GHSA-f9g8-6ppc-pqq4 covers the same apiCall ServiceAccount token injection as GHSA-8wfp-579w-6r25 at pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go. The kyverno admission controller exercises this executor during policy evaluation. Upstream fix is in Kyverno 1.16.4; the packaged 1.15.3 and 1.16.3 lines are below that and no 1.15.x backport has been published. Tracking upstream.

The kyverno admission controller loads ConfigMap context via pkg/engine/context/loaders/configmap.go, whose NewConfigMapLoader does not validate the target namespace (CVE-2026-41068). Upstream fix is in Kyverno 1.17.2; the packaged 1.15.3, 1.16.3, and 1.17.1 lines are below that and no 1.15.x or 1.16.x backport has been published. Tracking upstream.

The kyverno admission controller evaluates policies at admission time and exercises the apiCall executor at pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go when policies use apiCall service mode. Upstream fix is in Kyverno 1.16.4; the packaged 1.15.3 and 1.16.3 lines are below that and no 1.15.x backport has been published. Tracking upstream.

GHSA-f9g8-6ppc-pqq4 covers the same apiCall ServiceAccount token injection as GHSA-8wfp-579w-6r25. kyverno-reports-controller instantiates the apiCall executor via cmd/reports-controller/main.go and can therefore reach pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go when a reported policy uses apiCall service mode. Upstream fix is in Kyverno 1.16.4; the packaged 1.15.3 and 1.16.3 lines are below that and no 1.15.x backport has been published. Tracking upstream.

kyverno-reports-controller re-evaluates policies via factories.DefaultContextLoaderFactory to build policy reports and can therefore reach the ConfigMap loader at pkg/engine/context/loaders/configmap.go (CVE-2026-41068) when reported policies use a configMap context. Upstream fix is in Kyverno 1.17.2; the packaged 1.15.3, 1.16.3, and 1.17.1 lines are below that and no 1.15.x or 1.16.x backport has been published. Tracking upstream.

kyverno-readiness-checker (cmd/readiness-checker/) is a lightweight Kubernetes readiness probe binary. Its dependency graph does not include github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/engine/context/loaders or github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/engine/apicall, so the vulnerable ConfigMap context loader at pkg/engine/context/loaders/configmap.go (CVE-2026-41068) is not compiled into this binary.

kyverno-init (cmd/kyverno-init/main.go) is a one-shot upgrade/cleanup job that removes stale PolicyReport and ClusterPolicyReport resources via the Kubernetes client. It does not instantiate the Kyverno policy engine, configure an apiCall executor, or call apicall.NewAPICallConfiguration. Although pkg/engine/apicall appears in the vendored dependency graph via transitive imports, the vulnerable Authorization-header injection at pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go is never reached at runtime.

GHSA-f9g8-6ppc-pqq4 covers the same apiCall ServiceAccount token injection as GHSA-8wfp-579w-6r25 at pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go. kyverno-cli runs outside a Kubernetes pod; /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token does not exist, executor.getToken() returns the empty string, and the req.Header.Add("Authorization", ...) sink at pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go:151 is never reached. The CLI cannot leak an admission-controller ServiceAccount token it does not possess.

kyverno-readiness-checker (cmd/readiness-checker/) is a lightweight Kubernetes readiness probe binary. Its dependency graph does not include github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/engine/context/loaders or github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/engine/apicall, so the vulnerable ConfigMap context loader at pkg/engine/context/loaders/configmap.go (CVE-2026-41068) is not compiled into this binary.

kyverno-cli compiles the ConfigMap context loader at pkg/engine/context/loaders/configmap.go via cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/store/contextloader.go and exercises it when the CLI is run against a cluster (e.g., kyverno apply --cluster). The CVE-2026-41068 attacker model (namespace-scoped admin abusing Kyverno's privileged ServiceAccount) does not directly apply to CLI invocations, which run with the invoking user's kubeconfig credentials rather than an elevated Kyverno SA. Upstream fix is in Kyverno 1.17.2; the packaged 1.15.3, 1.16.3, and 1.17.1 lines are below that and no 1.15.x or 1.16.x backport has been published. Tracking upstream pending confirmation that no CLI-specific exploit path exists.

kyverno-cli runs outside a Kubernetes pod. The apiCall executor's token-injection branch at pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go:147-152 guards on `req.Header.Get("Authorization") == ""` and `token != ""`; executor.getToken() reads /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, which does not exist in a CLI runtime. getToken() therefore returns the empty string and the req.Header.Add("Authorization", ...) sink is never executed. kyverno-cli cannot leak an admission-controller ServiceAccount token it does not possess.

Although pkg/engine/apicall appears in the vendored dependency graph via transitive imports, the vulnerable Authorization-header injection at pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go is never reached at runtime.
